cases.title: An array-valued channel is aggregated per position; count counts reads, not elements
cases.intent: For array values aggregationSets builds one set per element position across the buffered reads (Aggregator.kt:97-127) and returns a list of per-position results (:197), so a 3-element counter over a Size 4 window gives min/max/sum/avg as 3-element lists, while count is the number of buffered reads (:414) and values lists the 4 arrays. For window k with b = 12(k-1): min [b, b+1, b+2], max [b+9, b+10, b+11], sum [4b+18, 4b+22, 4b+26] as integers, avg [b+4.5, b+5.5, b+6.5].

cases.title: A change filter feeding an aggregation yields an exact values array per window
cases.intent: Reads whose channels are all filtered out produce nothing (ScheduleReader.kt:339), so the aggregator only receives passing reads. A 0..20 counter behind an Absolute 5 change filter passes exactly 0,5,10,15,20 per 21-read cycle, so each Size 5 window is exactly one cycle: values [0,5,10,15,20], count 5, min 0, max 20 - in every window, which also proves the filter state survives across windows.

cases.title: Aggregation Output is keyed by source/channel IDs (comma lists allowed); a Name-keyed Output silently yields messages without sources
cases.intent: Output keys are split on commas and trimmed (AggregationConfiguration.kt:42-50) and matched against source and channel IDs (:99-109), while the payload is written with the configured Names (ScheduleWriter.kt:199-229). So one 's1, s2' x 'c1,c2' entry aggregates four channels, which appear under the names PressSource/Pressure. An Output keyed by the Names instead matches nothing; no validation catches it and the aggregator still submits the empty aggregation map (ScheduleAggregator.kt:76-84), so a message with no 'sources' element is written per window.

cases.title: All 11 aggregation functions give exact values over disjoint size-based windows (Int and Double inputs, mode ties, first/last/values)
cases.intent: Every aggregation function on a counter whose window contents are known exactly: with no filters each channel is present on every read, so a Size 10 window is exactly 10 consecutive reads and windows are disjoint (Aggregator.kt:58-91, buffers cleared at :483). For window k of an Int counter from 1: count 10, sum 100k-45 as an integer (sum keeps integers as Long, :288-299), avg and median 10k-4.5 as Double, min 10k-9 and max 10k keeping the Int type, and population stddev sqrt(8.25) (:327-347). A Double counter step 0.5 gives sum 22.5 as Double. A 1,2,1,2 counter has a tie, so mode returns both values in first-occurrence order (:381-406). first/last/values carry the per-value timestamps (normalised). Consecutive windows prove no read is lost or counted twice.

assert.comment: window 2 starts right after window 1's max 4.5

cases.title: Aggregation Output precedence follows JSON key order, not specificity (known defect)
cases.intent: aggregationOutputs walks the Output map in JSON order and returns from inside the first (source, channel) entry that matches, exact or wildcard (AggregationConfiguration.kt:102-115); the specificity order built at :92-97 is only compared against that one entry. So the documented rule 'the best matching entry will be applied' (docs/core/aggregation-configuration.md:30-37, comment at :78-84) is dead: a wildcard listed before the specific entry wins. Three schedules with their own sources isolate three orderings; PC (specific first) is the control that works today.

knownDefect.summary: aggregationOutputs returns at the first matching Output entry in JSON order, so a wildcard listed before a specific source/channel entry overrides it

cases.title: The aggregation flush uses the depth of the last-iterated channel, so a filtered channel lets the others exceed Size (known defect)
cases.intent: Aggregator.add returns the timestamp count of whichever channel it stored last (Aggregator.kt:80, 90), and ScheduleAggregator flushes when that count reaches Size (ScheduleAggregator.kt:75). With a, then b, where b passes only every other read: read 0 stores {a} (a=1), read 1 stores {a, b} but b is last with depth 1, so no flush although a holds 2 values; read 2 flushes a with 3 values. After that the windows happen to realign to 2. Restricted to inprocess/uberjar: the defect depends on channel-map iteration order, and in IPC the channels cross a protobuf map whose order the protobuf spec does not guarantee.

knownDefect.summary: add() returns the buffered depth of the last channel iterated, so a channel missing from some reads delays the flush and the first window holds Size+1 values

cases.title: Aggregated envelope: an extra value level per function, function order kept, metadata kept; TimestampLevel has no effect (known defect)
cases.intent: An aggregated channel's value is a map from function name to {value[, timestamp]} (Aggregator.kt:448-479), in the order the Output lists them, and the source/channel Metadata and the schedule Metadata (which overrides the top-level one key by key) still apply. But the aggregated SourceOutputData is built without a timestamp (ScheduleAggregator.kt:76-82) and the reader bypasses buildOutputValues on the aggregated path (ScheduleReader.kt:340-352), so TimestampLevel is ignored: 'Both' yields no source or channel timestamp, while 'None' still yields first.timestamp. The docs say first/last/values timestamps depend on the schedule's TimestampLevel (docs/core/aggregation-configuration.md:118,122). Exact metadata is asserted, so the harness marker is not injected.

assert.comment: Schedule Metadata overrides the top-level Metadata per schedule only (ScheduleWriter.kt:148)

knownDefect.summary: Aggregated SourceOutputData is built without a timestamp and the aggregated path skips buildOutputValues, so TimestampLevel is ignored: Both gives no timestamps, None still gives first/last/values timestamps

cases.title: Aggregation Size 1 short-circuits: stddev returns the value, avg/median keep the integer type, mode becomes a timestamped scalar (known defect)
cases.intent: applyNumericAggregation returns the raw buffered value when the buffer holds one value (Aggregator.kt:177-180), bypassing the aggregation itself, and mode has its own size-1 branch that returns the value with its timestamp (:389-392). Size 1 is accepted (AggregationConfiguration.kt:289-295). With a constant 7: count 1, sum 7, min 7, max 7 and values are right, but stddev is 7 instead of 0.0 (the 'fewer than 2 values' guard at :331 is unreachable), avg and median are the Int 7 instead of 7.0, and mode is {value: 7, timestamp} instead of {value: [7]}.

knownDefect.summary: A 1-element buffer returns the raw value: stddev 7 instead of 0.0, avg/median Int 7 instead of 7.0, mode {value: 7, timestamp} instead of {value: [7]}

cases.title: Output ["*"] expands by data type (9 numeric, 5 non-numeric including first/last); avg on a String is dropped with an error
cases.intent: A wildcard output list expands to NUMERIC_AGGREGATIONS for a numeric channel and NON_NUMERIC_AGGREGATIONS otherwise (Aggregator.kt:617-631, 646-666), in that set order. So the numeric channel gets 9 functions (no first/last) and the String channel gets first, last, mode, count, values - the docs list only count, mode and values for non-numeric data (docs/core/aggregation-configuration.md:73-75). An explicit avg on a String logs 'aggregation requires numeric datatype' (:183-187) and, being null, 'returns a null value' (:471), so only count remains.

cases.title: Aggregation-output transformations (named and wildcard) versus channel transformations; array-valued aggregates get rewrapped (known defect)
cases.intent: An aggregation's Transformations map applies a transformation to one aggregated output after aggregation (Aggregator.kt:583-599; matching at AggregationConfiguration.kt:137-183), while a channel's own Transformation runs before buffering (ScheduleReader.kt:331). XA: only c.avg is transformed (100k-45.0), c.min/max stay raw Ints, and the channel-transformed ct aggregates already-multiplied values. XB: the '*' output wildcard transforms every output, including count (100) and the integer sum (1000k-450). XC: transforming an array-valued aggregate (an array channel's min, a mode list) goes through applyTransformationOnArray, which wraps every element in a ChannelReadValue (:567-576) that asChannelOutputData then serializes as an object (:499-503): [{value: 0}, ...] instead of [0, ...].

knownDefect.summary: applyTransformationOnArray wraps each transformed element in a ChannelReadValue, so an array-valued aggregate is serialized as [{value: x}, ...] instead of [x, ...]
